answer: Forging 566 of these means building 566 separate practice records from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. The defence rests on dispensing optician registration with practice record: years served at one optical practice. The ridge check is what stops the copy-paste farm: Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The ember record is public, the haven cost is per identity, and 566 aliases cost 566 times one honest seat.
